heroHeadline: UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration Hits 5-Year Midpoint: Pledges Soar, Delivery Lags; Amazon Degradation Worsens Beyond Official Metrics
heroSubtitle: As World Biodiversity Day 2026 approaches (May 22), the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration marks its approximate halfway point — with political commitment at historic highs but verified delivery far behind pledges. A Nature study warns the Amazon could reach an irreversible tipping point at 22–28% deforestation (currently ~18%), while new research confirms that hidden degradation from selective logging, fire, and drought now biologically compromises ~40% of remaining Amazon forest — damage invisible in official deforestation metrics. Separately, a peer-reviewed study in the Journal of Applied Ecology found the globally popular Miyawaki dense-planting urban mini-forest method lacks robust scientific evidence for its headline claims, calling for standardized monitoring before further scaling. On the positive side, Octopus Energy committed $500M to Living Carbon for Appalachian mine-site reforestation — one of the largest institutional nature-based carbon investments disclosed to date.
footerNote: Data sourced from UNEP, FAO, UNCCD, IUCN, WRI Global Forest Watch, INPE, and Tier 2 science outlets. Pledge figures reflect commitments; verified restoration is substantially lower.
